assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, with Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's Sr clocks reaching around 1e-18 uncertainty, opened a new regime of precision measurement. The idea is original and clean, and the impact is lasting: redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and searches for dark matter. From an atomic-physics view the control of light shifts and the clock-transition physics are both elegant and demanding.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the original magic-wavelength lattice proposal and early demonstrations; Ye built the leading high-accuracy Sr clocks and the fine-structure-level systematic control, and also advanced frequency-comb links. Two names give a coherent prize configuration. Other groups contributed (e.g. Yb clocks, Hall and Haensch comb technology, already recognised in 2005), but they are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent confirmation across many laboratories, with clocks agreeing at the 1e-18 level and operating continuously. The redefinition of the SI second is still pending, but the science is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to separate the lattice-clock concept from the later accuracy race.
Details of priority between Katori's proposal and parallel ideas are recalled from memory and not independently verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with cold atoms turned optical lattices into controlled many-body laboratories, covering the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, fermionic Hubbard physics, and single-site resolved quantum gas microscopy. The originality is high and the effect on many-body physics, including strongly correlated electron problems, is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and collaborators) provided the key theoretical proposal for bosons in optical lattices; Bloch and Greiner realised the Mott transition and the quantum gas microscope; Esslinger led fermionic Hubbard work. The group is larger than three, and Greiner's omission from my proposed trio is a genuine allocation difficulty; Bloch and Zoller are the most defensible core with Esslinger as the third.
assessment.maturity: Roughly two decades of independent confirmation from several groups. Interpretation is stable, although the strongest claims about solving open problems of high-Tc physics are not yet established. The Bose-Einstein condensation prize of 2001 and later cold-atom recognitions make the field familiar to the committee.
uncertainties: Credit split between theory proposals and the first experiments, and whether Greiner should displace someone.
Overlap with candidate B008, which may be a competing framing of the same underlying body of work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brings strong coupling between a single photon and an artificial atom into superconducting circuits, which underlies dispersive readout, gates and the modern superconducting quantum-computing platform. The conceptual clarity is high: it is cavity QED transferred to an engineered setting with large coupling strength. Impact is large and growing.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators with Girvin (not credited here) proposed the architecture; Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Schoelkopf and Wallraff as experimentalists plus Blais as theorist is a plausible trio, though the omission of Girvin and Devoret-adjacent contributors leaves an allocation gap.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed and reproduced across many labs. Timing is somewhat delicate because the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic tunnelling in circuits, and a close follow-on may feel redundant to some members.
uncertainties: Whether the 2025 prize makes recognition of this adjacent work premature or complementary.
Girvin and other theory contributors are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube observed a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and later a TXS 0506+056 association, opening neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. This is an observational milestone with clear physical meaning and an exceptional instrument built in the Antarctic ice.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual driver and project leader; Karle and Spiering held major scientific and instrument roles. A collaboration of hundreds makes the individual attribution subtle, and credit for the AMANDA predecessor and the 2013 analysis may be spread more widely than the three names.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed by multiple analyses and by other detectors in part. Source identification is still partial, with only one or two compelling associations, so the interpretation is incomplete but not unstable.
uncertainties: Extent to which individual attribution can be fairly narrowed in a large collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing-array evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, with the Hellings-Downs angular correlation, opens a new band of gravitational astronomy and probes supermassive black-hole binaries or exotic early-universe sources. The scientific value is high.
assessment.attribution: Several PTA collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, IPTA) announced results together in 2023, and the decisive contributions are dispersed over many people and decades of pulsar timing. The credited names give a possible but contestable subset; Hobbs, Kramer and Siemens represent distinct arrays.
assessment.maturity: The signal is at roughly 3 to 4 sigma in individual arrays; confirmation of the Hellings-Downs curve at high significance and identification of the source are still pending, so recognition is probably early.
uncertainties: Detection significance and the astrophysical origin of the signal remain unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade yields strongly interacting neutral-atom qubits and programmable arrays of tweezers, enabling quantum simulation and gate-based computation. It builds on atomic physics I know well, in which Rydberg interactions and their precise calculation play a central role. The concept is original and the impact on quantum technology is rising.
assessment.attribution: The blockade proposal came from Jaksch, Cirac, Zoller, Lukin and others, with Saffman and Walker contributing gate schemes; Browaeys and Lukin led the decisive experimental demonstrations. The credited trio omits original proposers, so attribution is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Strong demonstrations from several groups, but still developing; the field is moving quickly and long-term importance relative to other cold-atom platforms is not settled. Probably slightly early.
uncertainties: Priority among theory proposers who are not in the credited list.
Whether practical quantum advantage will change the weight of the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory in two dimensions gives exact results for critical phenomena, string worldsheet theory and many statistical models, and remains a unifying framework across statistical physics and high-energy theory. Its depth is very high.
assessment.attribution: Polyakov and Zamolodchikov (with Belavin, who is not credited) wrote the BPZ construction; Cardy brought central-charge and finite-size applications to critical phenomena. Missing credit for Belavin and others makes a clean configuration difficult.
assessment.maturity: The framework is thoroughly established and tested numerically and in real systems. Recognition is long overdue rather than premature, but the committee has historically favored work with direct experimental connection.
uncertainties: The credited list lacks Belavin and Friedan, Shenker and Qiu.
Weight placed on directly testable physics versus mathematical-physics structure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 confirmed the origin of electroweak symmetry breaking and is among the major results of particle physics. Clarity and importance are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize already recognised the theoretical prediction. The experimental discovery rests on thousands of collaborators and on the leadership and design contributions of the credited people, so assigning an individual configuration is the main obstacle; spokespeople and founders are plausible but contentious proxies.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two independent experiments and extensively measured in later runs. Recognition is long overdue but constrained by the prize rules on attribution.
uncertainties: Fair attribution in a very large collaboration.
The rule limiting the prize to three people versus the scale of the experimental effort.
